items.followUp: Give an example of a body moving with constant velocity while in equilibrium, and state why it is in equilibrium.

rubric.why: The question asks for an example of a body that is moving while in equilibrium.
rubric.description: Gives a valid example of a moving body in equilibrium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for an example such as a parachutist or raindrop falling at terminal velocity.

rubric.why: A body in equilibrium has zero resultant force; in the example, air resistance balances the weight.
rubric.description: States why the example is in equilibrium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the forces balance or the resultant force is zero.

modelAnswer: A parachutist falling at terminal velocity is moving but is in equilibrium.
The air resistance balances the weight, so the resultant force is zero and the parachutist moves with constant velocity.

items.followUp: A person pushes a wall, but it does not move. Is mechanical work done on the wall? Explain.

rubric.why: Mechanical work on the boat requires displacement in the direction of the applied force.
rubric.description: States whether mechanical work is done on the boat.

rubric.why: The boat is at rest relative to the shore, so its displacement relative to the shore is zero and the work done on it is zero.
rubric.description: Explains the answer using the boat's displacement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the boat has no displacement relative to the shore, so no mechanical work is done on it.

modelAnswer: No, no mechanical work is done on the boat relative to the shore.
The boat's displacement relative to the shore is zero, so W = F s = 0.
The man may expend effort, but the boat does not move relative to the shore.

items.followUp: Define pressure and write its SI unit. How is pressure related to force and area?

rubric.why: Force is described as a push or pull acting on a body.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying force as a push or pull.

rubric.why: Pressure is the normal force acting per unit area of a surface.
rubric.description: Defines pressure in a way that distinguishes it from force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that pressure is force per unit area.

modelAnswer: Force is a push or pull that can change or tend to change the state of motion or shape of a body.
Pressure is the normal force acting per unit area of a surface: P = F/A.
Force is measured in newtons, whereas pressure is measured in pascals (N/m²).
